The rewrite from `! grep -q ...` to `grep -q ... && exit 1` is a genuine fix, not a style change: under `set -euo pipefail` (line 2) bash exempts a `!`-prefixed pipeline from errexit, so the old negated assertion could never fail the script. The new form matches the repo idiom used throughout tests/go/test-pr-ready-review.sh.

findings.note: Misleading comment on a write path. internal/runchain/runchain_test.go:241 reads "Read-only path: there is nothing a Close error could tell the caller", but appendLine opens the file with os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_APPEND (line 237) and then WriteStrings to it (line 243). The swallowed Close error is harmless in practice (os.File writes are unbuffered syscalls, and this is a test helper), but the justification given is factually wrong and would mislead anyone reusing the pattern on a path where Close does report errors.

evidence.note: comment claims a read-only path
os.OpenFile with O_WRONLY|O_APPEND, i.e. a write path

findings.note: RenderPrompt discards format's error: `user, _ := format(template, values)` at internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:208. The declared ERR_PROMPT_TEMPLATE contract (spec docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:123) can therefore never surface a template defect: a future edit that introduces an unknown slot or a stray brace would return an empty user prompt with a nil error rather than an error. Today the templates are package constants and every slot is golden-tested, so this is latent only.

evidence.note: format error assigned to blank identifier
format returns ERR_PROMPT_TEMPLATE errors that no caller can observe

findings.note: Parse routes unknown kinds into the still-present branch. internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:336 uses `default:` rather than `case KindStillPresent:`, so Parse("typo-kind", raw) silently parses the text as a still-present verdict instead of reporting an unsupported kind. It is unreachable through Judge.Call today because RenderPrompt (prompts.go:194) rejects unknown kinds first, but Parse is exported and the two functions disagree on strictness. A related wrinkle: the fail closure at prompts.go:311 returns `kind == KindStillPresent` as the decision, so an unknown kind parsed as still-present would fail *open* (decision false) rather than closed.

evidence.note: default branch handles still-present and every unknown kind
RenderPrompt errors on an unknown kind, so the two entry points disagree

findings.note: The all_fixed gate's failure detail is misleading when nothing was ever found. converge.AllFixed (internal/fsm/converge/converge.go:26) deliberately treats an empty AllFound as NOT fixed, so the gate at internal/fsm/gate/gates.go:84 reports "0 of 0 bugs unfixed" for the empty case, which reads as a contradiction in the audit log instead of naming the actual reason (no bugs were ever recorded). Message-only; the gate decision itself is correct and intentional.

evidence.note: detail formats %d of %d, both zero when AllFound is empty
AllFixed requires len(AllFound) > 0 by design

findings.note: Investigated and dismissed: the match prompt is not fenced. RenderPrompt (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:172) populates `fenced` only for adjudicate and still-present, so match's golden_comment and candidate slots are injected raw even in product mode, and testdata/prompts/match.fenced.golden is byte-identical to match.calibration.golden. This looked like an untrusted-content injection gap, but it is the documented design: "`match` is never fenced" in docs/specs/2026-08-26-metareview-0.9.0-build-plan.md:53 (change C25) and docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:125. The identical goldens are the intended, tested outcome, and match compares a golden comment to a candidate string rather than raw diff text.

evidence.note: match sets no fenced slots
C25 states match is never fenced
